headline: The leverage is still there: Sunday liquidated $168M of longs, and open interest fell just 0.5%.
summary: Sunday's drop didn't flush the leverage, so another leg into 72–73K would trigger more liquidations. The three biggest buyer groups all have costs at 75–79K and are underwater, so rebounds there will meet break-even selling. Price-based selling is maxed out but on-chain loss-taking is still shallow, so sellers haven't capitulated; this week it's Nov 10 CPI and the 200-day average at 73,171.

overview.lead: Cost overhead and leverage underneath: the three biggest buyer groups are underwater, leverage hasn't cleared, and sellers still haven't capitulated.
points: Leverage didn't clear: Sunday liquidated $168M of longs, and open interest fell just 0.5%.
The costs sit overhead: short-term holders, Strategy and ETF holders stack at 75–79K, against a 74,738 close.
Price-based selling is maxed out, but on-chain loss-taking is under 40% of the June low. That isn't capitulation yet.
No exit rule moves, with the 200-day average 2% below; this week it's Nov 10 CPI and Nvidia earnings on Nov 17.

cycle.lead: The bull call holds, but every cycle gauge is weak: the 200-day average is still rising, and the weekly regime score and the Dawn index are soft but haven't turned down.
points: Bull day 31: 60 straight closes above the 200-day average, which is still rising.
Only 1 of 6 supporting lights is on, realized cap still growing; momentum, MVRV and exchange supply are all off.
The weekly regime score fell from 0.93 to 0.23, still early bull; the Dawn index is in Daybreak with heat 37. One reads trend, the other valuation, and neither has turned down.
At the last 30 days' pace, short-term holder cost crosses the True Market Mean around Dec 13; that's a straight-line extrapolation, not a forecast.

market.lead: Price is now below the 350-day average and short-term holder cost, and only about 2% above both the 200-day average and the leg-end line.
points: Selling pressure is full and momentum quality fell to 0.25, so the bottom combo fired (see the second finding).
Sunday's drop had volume behind it: two-thirds of normal, on a 3.5% daily range.
The leg-end line at 73,605 is just 1.5% below; a close under it starts a new down leg.
Five straight red weeks, and 14% off the September high.

deriv.lead: After the liquidations longs pay less but hold just as much; below 74,000 dealers sell into the drop, so a fall can speed up.

Dealers are estimated to sell below 74,000 (Deribit only); the estimated long-liquidation band is 72–73K, about 3% below.
Near-dated implied vol is now above longer-dated, so the market sees more risk right ahead.
$195M of bids sit at 74,000, all on Hyperliquid perps.

points: ETF 7 trading days to Nov 5: −$1.36B (The Block); Nov 6 adds a provisional −$412M.

Coinbase still trades at a discount (7-day average −0.15%), so US buyers aren't back.

findings.title: Leverage didn't clear: $168M liquidated, OI still at the 98th percentile
findings.lean_why: Price is down 9% in 30 days while leverage is up a tenth; on another leg down, liquidations are market sells and would amplify the fall.
findings.what: Sunday's drop flushed only a small part of the longs, and leverage overall is still high: after $168M of long liquidations, open interest fell just 0.5% and sits at the 98th percentile since 2021 (Coinalyze, Nov 8).
findings.why: Longs pay less but haven't left. Funding fell about 3.5 points in a day, so the rush into longs has cooled; but open interest is up a tenth in 30 days while price fell 9%. 76% of Binance accounts are long, also near the top. The exception: Hyperliquid's top 2,000 accounts lean short, so the long pile-up is in small and mid-sized accounts.
findings.alt: Not all of the open-interest growth is longs; some may be basis trades (long spot, short perps) or hedges. The long-account share counts accounts, not position size. Binance pushes only one liquidation record per second, so totals run low; good for comparing longs vs shorts, not for totals.
findings.history: When the long-account share gets this crowded, what follows has been weaker than usual. Since 2021 there were 27 cases, with a median of −4.5% 90 days later against +2% normally (Coinalyze).
findings.so: What changed is the cost: longs pay less funding and the rush has cooled. What didn't change is the position: the estimated long-liquidation bands at 72–73K and 70–72K are still there (Coinalyze, seven venues), and a drop into them would trigger market selling that can speed the fall. No change to the market phase or the exit framework.
findings.next: Two paths by Nov 15: open interest falls below 322,000 BTC (about −5%), meaning leverage left on its own and a drop is less likely to be amplified, which refutes this; 7-day long liquidations top $800M, meaning leverage was flushed by liquidations and the fall was amplified, which confirms it.

findings.title: Bottom combo fired, but loss-taking is under 40% of the June low
findings.lean_why: Past bottom combos did better than usual over three months but worse within one; loss-taking is shallow this time, so it cuts both ways.
findings.what: Price-based selling is maxed out, but sellers haven't capitulated: our selling pressure is at 100 and momentum quality at 0.25, so the bottom combo fired; yet the latest realized-loss peak is only 4.8 basis points of market cap, against 13.2 at the June 30 low (Bitview).
findings.why: More holders are at a loss on paper, fewer are actually selling at one. 74% of short-term holders are underwater, the most in 30 days, yet their realized losses fell from 4,177 to 3,875 BTC (CheckOnChain, Nov 8). On the other side, long-term holders who do sell are taking losses too, with LTH-SOPR at 0.94 (Bitview).
findings.alt: Selling pressure uses only closing prices, so a slow grind lower can also max it out. In the ETF era much of the turnover happens in stock markets, off-chain, so on-chain loss-taking may run shallow even when sellers have given up.
findings.history: After a bottom combo, price has usually fallen further before working its way out. Since 2012 there were 21 cases: a median 9% drop while the combo lasted, then a median +15% three months later, better than the usual +10%.
findings.so: This is not a buy signal: price-based weakness is maxed out, but there's been no June-style burst of loss-taking, and past real lows usually came after one. No change to the market phase or the exit framework.
findings.next: Two paths by Nov 15: short-term holder realized losses top 5,000 BTC, or STH-SOPR falls below 0.985, meaning loss-taking is growing and sellers are starting to capitulate, which refutes 'shallow loss-taking'; if neither happens, loss-taking stays shallow and the combo takes longer to count.

findings.title: The three big buyer groups' costs stack at 75–79K, all underwater now
findings.lean_why: All three main buyer groups have costs overhead, so rebounds there meet break-even selling; below, coin supply is thin down to 64K, with no thick support on the way.
findings.what: Break-even sellers above, no thick support below: short-term holder cost 75,881, Strategy 75,451 and estimated ETF holder cost 79,039 all sit above the 74,738 close (Bitview, TechFlow, The Block estimate, Nov 5–8).
findings.why: The costs are all overhead. Short-term holders hold 3.72M BTC at an average cost of 75,219, thickest at 76K and 80K (CheckOnChain, Nov 8); the True Market Mean at 77,563 is also 4% above. Long-term holders' cost is 48,833, deep in profit, and their net selling is narrowing, so they aren't the main sellers.
findings.alt: ETF holder cost is our estimate from flows and excludes GBTC; Strategy's cost is the company's own figure, and a paper loss doesn't mean it will sell. On-chain costs are per-UTXO, so exchange wallet reshuffles count as turnover.
findings.history: This cycle's drawdown is far shallower than the last three: 398 days after the top it's down 40%, while the past three cycles were down 75–82% at the same point (only three cycles of data). Price has hugged short-term holder cost for 4 days.
findings.so: Rebounds into 75.5–79K meet break-even selling first. Below, there's no thick cost zone from 74K to 66K: at a 66,000 close, short-term holders at a loss would be only about 50K BTC more than at 70,000, jumping to 3.11M only at 64,000 (CheckOnChain, Nov 8). Price tends to move fast where coin supply is thin. No change to the market phase or the exit framework.
findings.next: Two paths by Nov 15: a close back above 76,000, over short-term holder and Strategy cost, refutes this; a close below 72,200, under the 200-day average and the liquidation band, confirms the costs overhead have turned into resistance.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: BTC about −10% from the September high, retesting the August breakout; STH supply in profit fell from ≥97.5% to about 38%; true market mean 77.7K, STH cost basis 75.7K, 200-day MA inside the 73–76K band, long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K; after the past three midterms BTC fell another 15–50% within 2–10 weeks. Conclusion: holding 73–76K is a healthy reset within the August uptrend; a break below 73K points to a longer consolidation.
items.meaning: The Nov 8 close of 74,738 is still inside its 73–76K band, and the intraday low of 73,444 touched the bottom edge; its "break below 73K" nearly coincides with our hedge line at 73,171. Midterm history has only 3 cases, so we do not use it.
